hints: Calculate the class width for each interval: 20, 20, 10, 10, 40.
Calculate frequency density for each interval using $\text{Frequency density} = \frac{\text{Frequency}}{\text{Class width}}$.
Plot rectangular bars on linear scales for time $t$ on the horizontal axis and frequency density on the vertical axis.
walkthrough:
Calculate the class width and frequency density (FD) for each interval:
- $0 \le t < 20$: Width $= 20$, Frequency $= 32 \implies \text{FD} = \frac{32}{20} = 1.6$
- $20 \le t < 40$: Width $= 20$, Frequency $= 46 \implies \text{FD} = \frac{46}{20} = 2.3$
- $40 \le t < 50$: Width $= 10$, Frequency $= 96 \implies \text{FD} = \frac{96}{10} = 9.6$
- $50 \le t < 60$: Width $= 10$, Frequency $= 52 \implies \text{FD} = \frac{52}{10} = 5.2$
- $60 \le t < 100$: Width $= 40$, Frequency $= 24 \implies \text{FD} = \frac{24}{40} = 0.6$
Set up the horizontal axis for Time $t$ (minutes) covering $0$ to $100$ with a linear scale.
Set up the vertical axis for Frequency density covering $0$ to $10$ with a linear scale.
Draw contiguous rectangular blocks corresponding to the calculated boundaries and heights.
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Compute frequency density for grouped continuous data.
Because the class intervals have unequal widths, the heights of the histogram bars must represent frequency density:
$$\text{Frequency Density} = \frac{\text{Frequency}}{\text{Class Width}}$$

Tabulate:
- Interval $[0, 20)$: Width $= 20$, Freq $= 32 \implies \text{FD} = \frac{32}{20} = 1.6$
- Interval $[20, 40)$: Width $= 20$, Freq $= 46 \implies \text{FD} = \frac{46}{20} = 2.3$
- Interval $[40, 50)$: Width $= 10$, Freq $= 96 \implies \text{FD} = \frac{96}{10} = 9.6$
- Interval $[50, 60)$: Width $= 10$, Freq $= 52 \implies \text{FD} = \frac{52}{10} = 5.2$
- Interval $[60, 100)$: Width $= 40$, Freq $= 24 \implies \text{FD} = \frac{24}{40} = 0.6$

Step 2: Draw the histogram.
- Horizontal axis: Time $t$ (minutes), marked from $0$ to $100$ with uniform spacing.
- Vertical axis: Frequency density, marked from $0$ to $10$ with uniform spacing.
- Draw adjacent bars without gaps between consecutive classes matching the widths and calculated heights.

ai_rubric.Constructing Histograms: Calculates frequency densities 1.6, 2.3, 9.6, 5.2, 0.6 and draws correct histogram with labelled axes. For this part: Draw a histogram to represent this information.

skill_tags: Estimating Standard Deviation from Grouped Data

hints: Find the midpoint $m$ of each class interval: 10, 30, 45, 55, 80.
Calculate $\sum f m$ and $\sum f m^2$ using frequencies $32, 46, 96, 52, 24$ with total $\sum f = 250$.
Calculate the mean $\bar{t} = \frac{\sum f m}{250}$ and variance $s^2 = \frac{\sum f m^2}{250} - \bar{t}^2$, then take the square root.
walkthrough:
Compute the variance and standard deviation:
$$s^2 = \frac{549\,900}{250} - (43.2)^2 = 2199.6 - 1866.24 = 333.36$$
$$s = \sqrt{333.36} \approx 18.258 \approx 18.3\text{ minutes}$$

ai_rubric.Estimating Standard Deviation from Group: Finds sum(fm) = 10800, mean = 43.2, sum(fm^2) = 549900, variance = 333.36, and standard deviation = 18.3 minutes. For this part: Calculate an estimate for the standard deviation of these times.
